assumptions: PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, and S3 are modeled as integer input flags because the NL explicitly calls them request/sensing inputs; their triggers are encoded as guards rather than pyfcstm events.
The hbrg output is encoded as 0 for stop, 1 for upward drive, and -1 for downward drive; the NL did not specify numeric output values.
Outstanding request memory and request clearing are not modeled because the NL only names request inputs and transitions, not latch/clear behavior or priority rules for simultaneous requests.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init: verifies initial dispatch lands on F1 with stop output, and with no requests the controller remains stopped on F1.
scenario_results.name: default_initial_floor1_idle_no_request

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: PS2 from F1 drives upward to MU2, S2 stops at F2, then outstanding PS1 immediately drives downward to MD1 and S1 returns to F1.
scenario_results.name: f1_request_f2_arrive_then_request_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: PS3 from F1 must target MU3 for upward travel to floor 3, and S3 arrival must stop at F3.
scenario_results.name: f1_request_f3_arrival

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: PS3 from F2 must select upward MU3, and S3 arrival must complete at F3 with stop output.
scenario_results.name: f2_request_f3_arrival

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: PS1 from F3 must select downward MD1, and S1 arrival must complete at F1 with stop output.
scenario_results.name: f3_request_f1_arrival

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: PS2 from F3 must select downward MD2, and S2 arrival must complete at F2 with stop output.
scenario_results.name: f3_request_f2_arrival

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: while in upward MU3, absence of S3 must not falsely complete arrival, and upward drive output remains asserted.
scenario_results.name: motion_without_arrival_sensor_does_not_stop

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: Reset from an upward motion context must force the controller to F1 and stop the drive.
scenario_results.name: reset_from_up_motion_forces_floor1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: Reset from a floor context other than F1 must force the controller back to F1 with stop output.
scenario_results.name: reset_from_floor3_forces_floor1

evidence: NL requires floor states F1/F2/F3 and motion states MU2/MU3/MD1/MD2; DSL defines all seven leaf states.
NL specifies F1->MU2 on PS2, F1->MU3 on PS3, F2->MU3 on PS3, F2->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD2 on PS2; DSL implements these guarded transitions.
NL specifies MU2+S2->F2, MU3+S3->F3, MD1+S1->F1, MD2+S2->F2; DSL implements these guarded transitions.
NL says reset forces controller back to floor 1; DSL has `! * -> F1 :: Reset`.
DSL sets hbrg=0 in floor states, hbrg=1 in upward motion states, and hbrg=-1 in downward motion states.
findings.summary: The DSL closely matches the NL-required elevator FSM states, request-triggered motion transitions, arrival-sensor completion transitions, reset-to-F1 behavior, and hbrg stop/up/down output distinctions.

evidence: GroundingMap marks all seven states, six request transitions, four arrival transitions, initial transition, reset transition, and hbrg actions as required and mapped.
inspect_model_to_json_summary reports 7 leaf states, 11 normal transitions, 7 forced reset transitions, 1 event, 7 variables, and 7 actions.
sim_summary reports 9/9 scenarios passed, including F1->F2, F1->F3, F2->F3, F3->F1, F3->F2, motion-without-arrival, and reset cases.
findings.summary: Required state, transition, input, reset, and output components are represented. Simulation covers the principal requested paths and reset cases.

evidence: DSL declares PS1/PS2/PS3/S1/S2/S3/hbrg uniformly as `def int`.
design_diagnostics_summary separately infers PS1/PS2/PS3/S1/S2/S3 as external input candidates, while hbrg is an output written by enter actions.
Diagnostics include W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for external inputs and W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for hbrg; these are advisory and expected under the current encoding, but indicate weak role typing.
findings.summary: External inputs and pure output are all declared as mutable `def int` variables, so role separation is implicit rather than structural.

evidence: From F1, both `PS2 > 0` and `PS3 > 0` may be true; DSL contains two enabled transitions with no explicit priority rule.
From F2, both `PS1 > 0` and `PS3 > 0` may be true; DSL contains two enabled transitions with no explicit priority rule.
GroundingMap source_summary states outstanding request memory, request clearing, and priority rules for simultaneous requests are not modeled because the NL did not specify them.
findings.summary: The model does not specify priority or tie-breaking for simultaneous floor requests, but the NL also does not define those semantics, so this is a non-blocking underspecification rather than a fidelity failure.

evidence: sim_summary reports all 9 scenarios passed, but scenario samples focus on single requested target paths and selected reset contexts.
No sampled scenario explicitly checks behavior when competing request guards are simultaneously true at F1, F2, or F3.
Reset is sampled from MU2 and F3, while the forced reset transition applies from all leaf states.
findings.summary: The passing simulation suite validates the main mapped paths but uses relatively direct hot-start scenarios and does not fully probe nondeterministic simultaneous-request behavior or every reset source context.

evidence: NL says hbrg distinguishes upward drive, downward drive, and stop conditions, but does not assign numeric values.
GroundingMap source_summary explicitly assumes hbrg=0 for stop, hbrg=1 for upward drive, and hbrg=-1 for downward drive.
DSL uses those assumed numeric encodings consistently in state enter actions.
findings.summary: The grounding is mostly strong, but the numeric encoding of hbrg values is an assumption rather than an explicit NL requirement.

warning_budget_exhausted is empty.
sim_summary has ok=true and 9/9 scenarios passed.
The model is not an empty shell: it contains all grounded required states, guarded transitions, reset handling, and hbrg actions.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate.
